tests.question: Does time-resolved reconstruction materially change or remove the static ring morphology inferred from Earth-rotation synthesis?
tests.observable: Differences between static and time-resolved reconstructions in closure fit, ring diameter, width, circularity, and temporal residual structure.
tests.method: Execute pinned dynamic-imaging and static-imaging methods on the same time-resolved observables; compare held-out closure quantities and morphology using registered temporal and image contracts.
tests.support_condition: Dynamic modeling yields substantially better held-out data fit and produces morphology outside the static reconstruction's reviewed stability region.
tests.refutation_condition: Dynamic and static methods produce compatible ring morphology and held-out fit within reviewed tolerances across time segments.
tests.inconclusive_condition: Temporal resolution is insufficient, dynamic regularization dominates the result, or both methods share the same static bias.

tests.question: Can plausible source variability create a stable static ring when the instantaneous source lacks comparable ring morphology?
tests.observable: False stable-ring recovery rate from synthetic time-variable, non-ring instantaneous source sequences under the actual sampling schedule.
tests.method: Generate preregistered variable source movies, sample them with the observed time coverage, reconstruct them as static and dynamic sources, and score false ring recovery.
missing_prerequisites: blind static and dynamic reconstruction procedure
tests.support_condition: Plausible non-ring source movies frequently generate static ring morphology comparable to M87 above the reviewed false-recovery threshold.
tests.refutation_condition: The static pipeline rarely creates comparable rings from plausible non-ring movies and accurately recovers injected ring movies.
tests.inconclusive_condition: The variability ensemble does not cover plausible source dynamics or the sampling/systematic model is incomplete.

independence_requirements: Dynamic and static algorithms should be independently implemented or dependency overlap must be disclosed.
Temporal regularization and source-movie ensembles must be registered before final evaluation.
At least one time segment or observable set must be held out.
False-recovery thresholds must be set before inspecting M87 results.
limitations: Static-morphology stability does not prove that the source is time invariant.
Dynamic-model flexibility can improve fit without yielding a uniquely correct movie.
